answer: A trust-graph protocol resists Sybil attacks by treating each agent as a vertex in an interaction network. Random-walk routing confines fake identities behind topological bottlenecks unless validated by real commerce, such as bilateral escrows for timber or carved ivory. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of building authentic relational trust with honest peers per identity. However, this restricts legitimate newcomers and fails if an adversary compromises key bridge nodes.
